title: Ordinary scalar cycle coordinates and evaluation
statement: Let W be a scheme, w∈U an affine open, m a natural number, and d a vector in Γ(W,U)^m. Let K be a strictly perfect complex on the localized site over U [def-pc-perfect-complex], with section bases e0:Γ(K^0)≃Γ(W,U) and e1:Γ(K^1)≃Γ(W,U)^m. Assume e1(d_K^0(e0 inverse(a)))=a d for all a and every d_i evaluates to zero in κ(w) [def-weil-residue-field]. Put p:Spec κ(w)→U equal to the open lift [def-sc-picard-derived-model-sections], and use ordinary tensor pullbacks and cycles G_K of [def-sc-picard-ordinary-model-cycles]. There is an additive equivalence b from raw morphisms Hom(t*O_W,p*A(K^0)), t:Spec κ(w)→W, to κ(w). Every such morphism lies in G_K(t,p). For every neighbourhood V⊆U of w, every equality p_V;(V→U)=p, and every a∈Γ(W,V) with a(d|V)=0, there exists x∈G_K(V.ι,V→U) whose ordinary restriction along p_V has b-coordinate a(w). No derived-category instance, derived object, or negative-degree vanishing is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0BF2, degree-zero cycle lifting; Tag 06Z0, ordinary affine tilde/Gamma adjunction in its proof; Tag 0096, tensor adjunction

proof.text: Apply raw coordinates to obtain b and b1 at the residue point, c and c1 on smaller opens, the two differential formulas, and residue naturality. Each evaluated coefficient is zero by hdw; the outgoing coordinate of every raw residue morphism is therefore zero. Injectivity and preservation of zero of b1 give membership in the cycles kernel. For a scalar a on V take the inverse image of a under c(V). Its coordinate is a, so the open differential formula and the scalar annihilation hypothesis make its outgoing coordinate zero. Injectivity and preservation of zero of c1(V) show it is a cycle. Naturality and the inverse identity show that its residue restriction has coordinate a(w).

proof_origin.description: C1 reduction to raw-coordinate differential formulas, then inverse-coordinate cycle construction and scalar vanishing.

theorem picard_ordinary_scalar_coordinates
    (W : Scheme.{v}) (w : W)
    (U : W.Opens) (hwU : w ∈ U) (hU : IsAffineOpen U)
    (m : ℕ) (d : Fin m → Γ(W, U))
    (K : CochainComplex
      (SheafOfModules.{v} ((moduleRings W.toRingedSpace).over U)) ℤ)
    (hK : IsStrictlyPerfect W U K)
    (e0 : (K.X 0).val.obj (.op (Over.mk (𝟙 U))) ≃ₗ[Γ(W, U)] Γ(W, U))
    (e1 : (K.X 1).val.obj (.op (Over.mk (𝟙 U))) ≃ₗ[Γ(W, U)] (Fin m → Γ(W, U)))
    (hd : ∀ a : Γ(W, U), e1 ((K.d 0 1).val.app (.op (Over.mk (𝟙 U))) (e0.symm a)) = a • d)
    (hdw : ∀ i, W.evaluation U w hwU (d i) = 0) :
    let p := picardResidueLift W w U hwU
    ∃ b : ((Modules.tensorPullback (W.fromSpecResidueField w)).obj
        (SheafOfModules.unit (moduleRings W.toRingedSpace)) ⟶
          (Modules.tensorPullback p).obj ((Modules.overEquiv U).functor.obj (K.X 0))) ≃+
            W.residueField w,
      (∀ f, f ∈ picardOrdinaryModelCycles W U K (W.fromSpecResidueField w) p) ∧
      ∀ (V : W.Opens) (hwV : w ∈ V) (hVU : V ≤ U)
        (hs : picardResidueLift W w V hwV ≫ W.homOfLE hVU = p) (a : Γ(W, V)),
        (a • (fun i ↦ W.presheaf.map (homOfLE hVU).op (d i)) = 0) →
        ∃ x : picardOrdinaryModelCycles W U K V.ι (W.homOfLE hVU),
          b (picardOrdinaryModelRestriction W U K (picardResidueLift W w V hwV)
            V.ι (W.fromSpecResidueField w) (W.homOfLE hVU) p
            (picardResidueLift_comp W w V hwV) hs x.val) =
              W.evaluation V w hwV a
